newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Wall Street lifts Singapore shares to a firm close.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street lifts Singapore shares to a firm close.

text.p: Singapore shares got a late boost from Wall Street to close higher on Monday, dealers said.
But volume was light as players wound down their activity ahead of Tuesday's shortened trading session.

The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index ended 15.85 points up at 2,218.45 after rising from its morning low of 2,196.97. Volume was around 57 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 223 to 84.
Dealers said Singapore's general elections on January 2 was unlikely to affect the market despite speculation of a 60 percent win by the ruling People's Action Party.

Warrants of Kim Eng Holdings and Uniphoenix Corporation led the actives with over 4.0 million shares each. Kim Eng warrants ended up Singapore $0.025 (US$0.018) at S$0.22 while Uniphoenix's warrants ended up S$0.42 at S$1.28.
Singapore Press Foreign led gainers, rising S$0.70 to S$27.50. Of its 92,000 shares traded, 43,000 were crossed at S$26.59 and S$26.80. Creative Technology rose S$0.70 to S$14.10 on 78,250 shares.
SIA Foreign and Total Access Communications were among losers, shedding S$0.20 and S$0.15 respectively.
